newsitem.title: DENMARK: Icopal "pretty sure" to bid for Phoenix.
newsitem.headline: Icopal "pretty sure" to bid for Phoenix.

text.p: Danish building materials firm Icopal said on Friday that it was "pretty" sure to bid for roadmaker Phoenix Contractors.
"We shall try and get an offer out today, but it's most likely that it will be at the beginning of next week," Icopal Managing Director Hans C. Andreasen told Reuters.
The Phoenix board on Thursday advised shareholders to accept an 820 million Danish crown offer by Norway's Rieber and Son, the highest of three offers pending Icopal's move.

Phoenix Chairman Henry Petersen said that an Icopal offer was unlikely to alter his recommendation of Rieber, which apart from making the highest bid has indicated that it will leave Phoenix relatively autonomous and keep layoffs to a minimum.
"If Icopal just outbids Rieber by five million crowns it is in poor taste. I don't think that on that basis we shall make a different declaration," he told Reuters.

Also bidding for Phoenix is heavyweight Danish construction and chemicals group Superfos which says it will not raise its offer of 808 million crowns but nevertheless does not consider itself out of the race.

Superfos is the favoured suitor of some of Phoenix's biggest institutional investors, such as pension fund ATP which holds around 10 percent. The fund also has a 12.6 percent stake in Superfos and close to 14.0 percent in Icopal.
An Icopal bid would automatically extend the deadline for further offers, currently March 7, for four weeks from the date of its proposal.
"It would be sad if we had to start another round of four weeks," Petersen said, adding that the battle was hampering the day-to-day running of his firm.
Rieber Managing Director Olav Daviknes said that he was surprised by the Icopal move but continued to buy Phoenix stock.
"We are still getting offers (to sell) and we are buying at the bid price, as we have done throughout. We are getting more offers than we did earlier," he said.
On Thursday Rieber stated that its stake was now 16.5 percent.
A fourth suitor, building contractor Marius Pedersen said last week that it would not raise its offer of 776 million crowns.
At 0930 GMT the most-traded Phoenix C-share was up five Danish crowns to 670, Rieber was unchanged at 235 Norwegian crowns, Superfos was up 12 Danish crowns to 787 and Icopal untraded at 1,520.
